sprint.intro:
Join the PyCon HK 2026 Development Sprint on Sunday, 15 November: a day of community collaboration on Python and open-source projects. Come ready to contribute, share ideas and learn together; this is not a taught workshop.

We are finalizing the projects and detailed arrangements. Read the Sprint Q&A to learn what to expect and how to prepare. Admission is free; register for Sprint Day separately from Conference Day.

On-site registration: 15 November 2026 at 10:00 Hong Kong time (UTC+8).
sprint.location: Hong Kong Institute of Information Technology (HKIIT), IVE (Lee Wai Lee), Tseung Kwan O

items.question: What is a Development Sprint?
items.answer:
A Development Sprint is a collaborative working session for open-source projects. Participants work with project maintainers and other contributors on useful tasks, share knowledge and learn by doing. Contributions can include code, tests, documentation, translation and other work that a project needs.

This is a community collaboration day, not a taught workshop or a step-by-step lesson. Come ready to contribute in a way that fits your experience.

items.question: What will I do on Sprint Day?
items.answer: Choose a project you are interested in, discuss a suitable task with its lead or contributors, and work on it together. Read the project's contribution and setup instructions when they are available. The detailed 2026 timetable and project arrangements will be announced when confirmed.

items.question: How is Sprint Day different from Conference Day?
items.answer: Conference Day on 14 November centres on talks, sessions and community activities. Sprint Day on 15 November focuses on working together on Python and open-source projects. They are separate activities and require separate ticket registration.

items.question: Who is Sprint Day for?
items.answer: Anyone interested in Python, open source or collaborative learning is welcome, including experienced contributors and people making their first contribution. You do not need to bring your own project. Look for a project whose goals and tasks match your interests.

items.question: Can Python beginners take part?
items.answer: Yes. The event welcomes newcomers as well as experienced contributors. Tell the project lead what you have tried and what you would like to learn. Depending on the project, a first task could involve documentation, translation, reproducing a problem or a small code change; available tasks and support vary by project.

items.question: What should I bring and prepare?
items.answer: Bring a laptop capable of running the tools for your chosen project, its charger and any adapters you need. Before the event, read the project's README, contribution guide and setup instructions when available, and prepare the accounts it uses, such as GitHub. Check the individual project's requirements before attending.

items.question: Can I come to observe and learn before contributing?
items.answer: If you want to observe, register for Sprint Day and speak with the project lead or organizing team about how to join the group. You can explain your interests and experience, learn how the project works and agree on a suitable way to participate. Please respect the group's working space and discussions.

items.question: What if I need to arrive late or leave early?
items.answer: Coordinate with the project lead or organizing team in advance. Let the group know when you expect to arrive or leave, so you can agree on a task and hand over any work. Check the confirmed timetable and entry instructions before travelling.

items.question: Is Sprint Day free, and do I need a separate ticket?
items.answer: Admission to PyCon HK 2026 is free, but Sprint Day on 15 November and Conference Day on 14 November require separate tickets. Use the registration button to register for the day or days you plan to attend. Optional contributions, T-shirts and PyNight are separate from free Sprint Day admission.

items.question: Can I propose my own project?
items.answer:
Yes. The published 2026 announcement invites proposals for Python and open-source Sprint projects. Use the call for Sprint projects and leads to describe your project, what you would like to work on and how others can contribute. Submitting a proposal does not by itself confirm a place in the programme.

The Sprint submission deadline is 14 November 2026 at 23:59 Hong Kong time (UTC+8).

items.question: How do I become a Sprint Lead?
items.answer: Use the call for Sprint projects and leads to submit your interest. A lead helps introduce the project, explain its setup and contribution process, and identify tasks that participants can work on together. Include the preparation participants will need and the kinds of contributions you can support.

items.question: Which projects and Sprint Leads are taking part?
items.answer: We are finalizing the projects, Sprint Leads and detailed arrangements. Confirmed information and project-specific setup instructions will be added to this page when available.

items.name: Open Home Foundation
items.description:
Smart homes should be private spaces where people can be themselves – not sources of data for Big Tech seeking to monetize personal information. The Open Home Foundation offers an alternative: a smart home built on privacy, choice, and sustainability for everyone.

Founded in 2024, the foundation is a tax-exempt Swiss non-profit that owns and governs more than 250 open source projects, including the Home Assistant home automation platform. It is funded by its commercial partners Nabu Casa and Apollo Automation, and independent donations. This structure ensures its core projects can never be sold, with resources invested in developing and promoting open standards and tools that serve its community of users, not advertisers or shareholders.

Beyond this work, the foundation advocates for the ethical use of smart home technology across the wider industry – engaging companies and the general public on the value of open standards and the vision of the Open Home.

items.name: Databricks
items.description:
Databricks is the data and AI company. Its Data Intelligence Platform brings together data, analytics, and AI on an open lakehouse foundation, helping organizations turn data into insights and build secure applications.

Founded by the original creators of Apache Spark™️, Delta Lake, MLflow, and Unity Catalog, Databricks is on a mission to simplify and democratize data and AI—helping businesses solve the world’s toughest problems.

items.name: Red Hat
items.description: Red Hat is the open hybrid cloud technology leader, delivering a trusted, consistent and comprehensive foundation for transformative IT innovation and AI applications. Its portfolio of cloud, developer, AI, Linux, automation and application platform technologies enables any application, anywhere—from the datacenter to the edge. As the world's leading provider of enterprise open source software solutions, Red Hat invests in open ecosystems and communities to solve tomorrow's IT challenges. Collaborating with partners and customers, Red Hat helps them build, connect, automate, secure and manage their IT environments, supported by consulting services and award-winning training and certification offerings.

patrons.intro: PyCon Hong Kong (PyCon HK) is a volunteer-run, not-for-profit conference committed to advancing Python and open source culture throughout Hong Kong and the wider Asian region. Your personal support as a Patron goes directly towards helping us:
benefits: Keep ticket prices free or affordable for everyone who wants to attend
Invite outstanding speakers to share their knowledge here in Hong Kong
Strengthen the Python and open source community and ecosystem locally
Sustain PyCon HK so it can expand with each passing year

paragraphs: PyCon Hong Kong (PyCon HK) is the leading Python conference in Hong Kong, bringing together Python enthusiasts to share their insights and foster collaboration. Among the 50+ PyCons hosted annually in various cities and countries worldwide, PyCon HK is proud to be one of them.

The founding of PyCon HK traces back to Mr. Sammy Fung, who drew inspiration from the PyCon APAC 2013 event in Tokyo. Sammy recognized that Hong Kong was missing out on this vital Python conference, despite PyCon being hosted in various Asian cities. Determined to fill this gap, Sammy collaborated with Open Source Hong Kong to organize the inaugural PyCon HK in 2015. Since then, PyCon HK has played a pivotal role in nurturing Python development and adoption within the city.

In 2026, PyCon Hong Kong welcomes Mr. Calvin Tsang as Chairman of PyCon HK 2026. An active member of the Python Asia Organisation community, Calvin regularly takes part in PyCon events across the region. A Technology Manager by profession, he has volunteered with PyCon HK since its very first edition. The combination of local commitment and international exposure allows him to bring together Python and open source community experience from around the world and open up new possibilities for PyCon HK.

Driven by dedicated volunteers, seasoned developers, educators, and tech innovators, PyCon HK 2026 continues its vibrant journey — celebrating the passion and creativity of the local and international Python community, and delivering an inspiring, high-impact event that connects Pythonistas, fosters open-source collaboration, and empowers innovation.

intro: PyCon HK 2026 presents an exceptional opportunity to connect with Hong Kong's most passionate Python developers, innovative tech leaders, and forward-thinking organizations.

As a sponsor, you'll be at the heart of Asia's premier Python conference, where cutting-edge ideas meet practical solutions. Join hundreds of enthusiastic developers, seasoned engineers, data scientists, and tech entrepreneurs who are shaping the future of technology in the region.

Your sponsorship doesn't just showcase your brand - it demonstrates your commitment to fostering innovation, supporting the open-source community, and driving technological advancement in Hong Kong and beyond.
